brief: Montenegro's supplier-and-scheme layer is dominated by two publishing actors: Mastercard, which runs a genuine country programme (MasterIndex, an annual ME cardholder survey since 2009, plus country milestone releases split across mastercard.me and mastercard.rs), and Payten/Asseco SEE, which is simultaneously the terminal and ATM service provider to ME banks, an independent ATM deployer via MoneyGet Crna Gora, and a WSE-listed issuer whose management reports explicitly name Montenegro as a key POS/ATM maintenance market. Visa, by contrast, publishes almost nothing country-specific for ME and is badly obscured in search by travel-visa noise, while AllSecure and Halcom leave no ME-specific press trail at all — AllSecure's Montenegrin footprint is visible only through merchant checkout boilerplate naming it alongside Hipotekarna banka as acquirer. The most productive routes are therefore vendor-to-bank pointers (Payten's SoftPOS-at-Hipotekarna release, Asseco case studies, ASEE filings), the local trade portal bankar.me which republishes vendor and scheme PR that never reaches vendor English sites, and bottom-up harvesting of merchant payment-terms pages and ATM locators. The main unmapped layer is card processing and switching for ME banks, and no ATM hardware OEM was found to name a Montenegrin customer — the hardware channel appears entirely intermediated through Payten.
